ModuleName: Functional Prototype Development and Testing Preparation
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Covers the key topics in the module — including transitioning from mockups to functional prototypes, design handoff, development environment setup, and testing preparation — serving as a topic outline to help learners and instructors navigate the scope and structure of the module.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: A navigational overview of the module's topics—covering the shift from static mockups to coded functional prototypes, what defines a functional prototype, and how these prototypes are prepared for usability testing—used by learners to preview and orient themselves to the module's scope before engaging with detailed content.

Artifacts.Name: From Mockup to Functional Prototype
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains why static mockups are insufficient for serious design validation and introduces the concept of functional prototypes, covering what makes a prototype 'functional,' the trade-offs involved, and how teams decide when to make the transition from static screens to working, interactive builds.

Artifacts.Name: Transition Strategies from Design to Code
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers strategies for translating polished design mockups into coded prototypes, addressing common pitfalls in the handoff process and providing guidance on how designers and developers can collaborate to maintain consistency between visual intent and functional behavior.

Artifacts.Name: Development Environment Setup and Use
Artifacts.Description: This reading walks through the decisions and steps involved in setting up a development environment for prototype building, including tool selection, collaboration practices, and workflow considerations that teams must address before writing any prototype code.

Artifacts.Name: Designing User Proficiency Surveys
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to design user proficiency surveys administered before usability sessions, covering why participant background—such as technology experience, domain familiarity, and prior product exposure—matters and how to craft survey questions that accurately capture it.

Artifacts.Name: Designing Usability Testing Protocols
Artifacts.Description: This reading describes how to design a usability testing protocol, covering the key components of the governing document that structures a user study, why standardization matters, and how to prevent facilitator drift and inconsistency across testing sessions.

Artifacts.Name: Integrating Prototype and Testing Preparation
Artifacts.Description: This reading addresses the challenge of aligning parallel workstreams—prototype development and test protocol design—so they are fully compatible when testing begins, offering guidance on coordination strategies to prevent mismatches between what the prototype does and what the test expects.
